title: Update every dependency: patches first, then each minor and major with its changelog
notes:
User's ask, 2026-11-27. Order:
1. All patch updates in one commit; pnpm check green.
2. Then each minor and each major one package at a time (or one tight family, e.g. @xterm/*): read its changelog/release notes between our version and the new one, apply what the app needs (renamed APIs, new defaults, deprecations we use, config changes), run pnpm check, one commit per package naming what changed and why.
Respect the existing pins: package-pins.test.ts and anything it names stays pinned unless its reason no longer holds, which you say in the commit. Electron majors: also read the breaking-changes doc and check the native-module path (node-pty) still rebuilds (pnpm install, make). If a major needs work beyond a few files, stop on that package, leave it out, and list it in the PR body with what it would take. pnpm install --frozen-lockfile must pass on the result. The PR body: a table of every package, from, to, and what changed in the app. The installed app needs a rebuild afterwards; do not touch the running app.
